football_evidence.question: Can Arizona contain Iowa State’s explosive runs?
football_evidence.assessment: Some measured evidence supports EdgeDesk’s lean toward Arizona, and its own breakdown accounts for about 0.0 of the 4.1 points, but not the full gap. It is a research question, not a bet.
supporting: When Arizona has the ball (big plays through the air): Arizona’s offense turns 14.7% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and Iowa State’s defense gives up explosive gains on 13.4% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.3%).

When Arizona has the ball (the passing game against the pass defense): Arizona’s offense averages 9.6 yards per pass attempt, and Iowa State’s defense allows 8.5 yards per pass attempt (FBS average 7.4).
When Arizona has the ball (third down): Arizona’s offense converts 53.7% of its third downs, and Iowa State’s defense allows opponents to convert 36.0% of their third downs (FBS average 39.7%).
When Arizona has the ball (the red zone): Arizona’s offense succeeds on 53.5% of its red-zone plays, and Iowa State’s defense allows success on 47.1% of opponent red-zone plays (FBS average 43.6%).
contradicting: When Iowa State has the ball (big plays on the ground): Iowa State’s offense turns 9.8% of its runs into explosive gains, and Arizona’s defense gives up explosive gains on 6.5% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.6%).
quarterbacks: Noah Fifita has completed 139 of 190 passes (73.2%) for 1,739 yards, 9.2 yards per attempt, 16 touchdowns and 4 interceptions in six games for Arizona, and has been sacked on 15 of 205 dropbacks.
Jaylen Raynor has completed 86 of 149 passes (57.7%) for 1,001 yards, 6.7 yards per attempt, 8 touchdowns and 3 interceptions in six games for Iowa State, and has been sacked on 8 of 157 dropbacks.

model: Arizona’s defense has to come out ahead on long runs: it gives up explosive gains on 6.5% of opponent runs, against an offense that turns 9.8% of its runs into explosive gains.
Arizona’s offense has to keep winning on big pass plays: it turns 14.7% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and Iowa State’s defense gives up explosive gains on 13.4% of opponent pass plays.
Arizona’s offense has to keep winning on long runs: it turns 6.8% of its runs into explosive gains, and Iowa State’s defense gives up explosive gains on 9.3% of opponent runs.
Home field has to be worth something close to the full 2.8 points EdgeDesk gives it.
